title: Basis on Which Rental Days, Drivers, Protection and Equipment Are Priced
content:
This note states how a Car Rental Rate Classes agreement is priced, from the day rate through to tax. Every
figure named is the figure published by the rate class booked.

## The rental days

The rental rate is charged day by day at the rate class's own daily rate, with the weekly rate substituted
whenever seven or more consecutive days are booked and the weekend rate applied to Saturdays and Sundays
within a rental of fewer than seven days. Seven consecutive days is the threshold at which the weekly rate
comes in, and a rental of six consecutive days is priced day by day with its Saturday and Sunday at the
weekend rate.

## When an optional item may be sold

An optional item is sold only while the rental record stands at confirmed or picked up. The rental record
is what decides this, not what the renter says about where the vehicle is; an item is not sold against a
rental standing at merely booked, returned, cancelled, a no-show or closed.

## Keeping the vehicle beyond the booked return

A vehicle kept beyond the booked return is charged the class's extra-hour fee for each hour past its grace
period, and once the hours charged reach the class's extra-day rate the extra day is charged instead of
further hours.

## Drivers

Additional drivers beyond the class's free count are charged per driver per rental day, and a driver never
named on the agreement is not insured at all.

## Protection and equipment

The collision damage waiver, theft protection, personal accident cover and roadside assistance are included
or charged per rental day exactly as the class prescribes, and a product included in the class is never also
charged.

Satellite navigation, child seats, snow chains and ski racks are charged at the class's own amounts, the
first two per day and the last two for the whole rental.

## Tax

Sales tax is applied to the rental total after every charge above has been added, and never to the deposit
hold. The tax figure is expressed to two decimal places.

## Hypothetical illustration of the day rate rule

A hypothetical booking of five consecutive days, two of them a Saturday and a Sunday, is priced at the
class's daily rate for the three weekday days and at its weekend rate for the other two, because five is
fewer than 7. A hypothetical booking of eight consecutive days passes the threshold, and the weekly rate is
substituted.
